title: Heuristic parameter inference, JSON schema annotation format, and human-friendly diagnostic hints
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: introduce a small, backwards-compatible extension to our JSON schema format that lets the runtime make conservative, explainable inferences and produce human-friendly diagnostic hints when tool/function call parameters fail validation. This ticket defines the annotation fields, runtime inference ordering, error taxonomy, and UX payloads that will be returned to callers and logged for observability.

Motivation: callers frequently provide near-correct inputs (string numbers, synonyms for enum values, omitted optional fields that can be defaulted). Strict rejection increases developer friction and causes noisy errors in production. We need a predictable, auditable approach that: 1) makes safe coercions by default for hosted API while exposing an opt-out, 2) surfaces suggested fixes in a structured way for programmatic handling, 3) maintains clear error codes for monitoring/alerts, and 4) preserves the canonical schema for compatibility across clients and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact schema annotation set (x-infer, x-default-suggestion, x-display-name, x-match-tolerance) that can be embedded in existing call parameter JSON schemas without breaking older validators.
Runtime implements a deterministic inference precedence: explicit cast rules -> safe coercion -> fuzzy match -> final rejection, with a log entry for each applied inference.
Errors returned for invalid parameters follow the new validation envelope: {code, message, field, suggestion, confidence, docs_link} (returned as top-level fields in HTTP/SDK error object).
Implement feature flag runtime: 'heuristic-param-inference' that can be enabled per-customer or per-route with a default of off for Dedicated/Private until validated.
Add telemetry events for inferred-coercion and suggestion-rejected with sample rate and include anonymized before/after values for debugging.
Provide a concise migration guide for SDKs and internal callsites describing how to opt-out and how to consume suggestions programmatically.
technical_design:
Schema annotations: we add prefixed fields under property schemas: 'x-infer': ['coerce_number','coerce_bool','parse_date','strip_whitespace'], 'x-default-suggestion': '<example JSON literal>', 'x-display-name': 'Friendly name for errors', 'x-match-tolerance': 'levenshtein:2|case-insensitive' or numeric 0.85 for similarity.

Runtime rules (ordered): 1) If value is missing and 'x-default-suggestion' exists, use default suggestion and mark 'auto_default' with low confidence. 2) If type mismatch and 'x-infer' includes a matching coercion, attempt typed coercion (string->int, numeric-with-commas->float, 'true'->bool). 3) If enum/choice mismatch, run deterministic fuzzy-match using configured tolerance (case-insensitive exact -> normalized whitespace -> simple levenshtein -> token set similarity). 4) If multiple candidate inferences, choose highest-confidence deterministic rule; do NOT apply probabilistic ML match unless explicit 'allow_ml' annotation is enabled. 5) If no safe inference, return structured error with suggestion(s) and a single canonical error code.

Error taxonomy: PARAM_MISSING, PARAM_TYPE_MISMATCH, PARAM_COERCION_APPLIED, PARAM_AMBIGUOUS_MATCH, PARAM_ENUM_MISMATCH. Each error must include: code, human_message, field_path, suggestion_list (0..n), confidence (0..1), inference_trace (string describing steps). Note: inference_trace is a short string not nested JSON (e.g., 'coerce_string_int->trim->accept').

Compatibility: older clients that don't understand annotations should ignore unknown fields. Annotations are prefixed with 'x-' to remain valid with standard JSON Schema tooling. For Dedicated/Private deployments, annotations can be toggled by admin flag.

Edge cases & safety: never coerce to enlarge permissions or change security-sensitive identifiers (x-infer must include 'disallow_coerce' for such fields). Provide an allowlist for coercion per-schema.

Observability: emit 'param_inference' event with tags: route, model, customer_id (hashed), field, applied_rule, outcome, latency_ms. Aggregate metrics for false_positive_inference and suggestion_accept_rate.
implementation_notes:
Backend: implement schema parser in runtime config loader and extend validator pipeline with an InferenceLayer that logs deterministic steps. Keep validator strictly ordered and deterministic to make rollbacks simple.

SDKs: add helpers to surface suggestions as typed exceptions and a utility to apply a recommended suggestion automatically.

Console: add a compact pane on per-route request samples showing 'Inferred parameters' with the before/after and a feedback button to mark incorrect inferences.

Security: gating - do not auto-coerce on fields with 'sensitive: true' or that are tagged as tokens/keys. Add unit tests for all coercion functions and integration tests exercising fuzzier match thresholds.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge schema and runtime plumbing behind feature flag (canary in host region 'us-west-2'). 2) Enable for internal developer orgs and collect telemetry for 2 weeks. 3) Enable for opt-in customers via console. 4) After acceptance criteria met and false-positive rate < 0.5%, flip default for hosted API; keep off for Dedicated/Private until security review completes. 5) Publish migration guide and SDK patches.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each coercion function (string->int, float normalization, bool recognition, date parse) and fuzzy-match combinations. Integration tests that simulate mismatched inputs and assert returned error envelope and logs. End-to-end canary: run a synthetic agent generating near-miss inputs and verify suggestion_accept_rate metric. Manual QA to validate human_message readability and that suggestions are actionable.
notes: Design had an initial review with Caroline (PM) and Rajiv (Design) on 2026-03-05 — main ask: keep messages short and provide 'apply suggestion' UX.
Avoid ML-based fuzzy matching in first iteration unless explicitly annotated; team wants deterministic behavior for audits.
Keep schema annotation set intentionally small to reduce surface area and docs burden.
